name: get_call_context
description: Call this first, exactly once, as soon as the call connects and before you say anything. Use dialed_line to pick the greeting (CA_MAIN means play the bilingual French/English greeting; US_MAIN means the standard English greeting), keep ani for the first authentication attempt, and use current_time_et and day_of_week for any time-based decisions. Never read the phone number or these field names aloud.

name: authenticate_merchant
description: Call this after the caller gives their Merchant ID and confirms your read-back. First attempt: pass merchant_id with ani from get_call_context, without asking the caller anything else. If that returns authenticated false, ask for the business zip or postal code and call again with merchant_id and postal_code. Do not call more than twice per call; after two failures, say you couldn't identify them and go to the main menu. On success, greet them by merchant_name and immediately call get_account_status. The caller is verified ONLY when the result contains authenticated: true; any other result, including an error, means not verified, so never say the account was found, never call get_account_status, and never share account details. If the result has tool_ran: false or an error, it is a system problem, not a failed try: call again with merchant_id and the second factor filled in. Never tell the caller their Merchant ID or any other value is incorrect or which value didn't match.

merchant_id.description: Merchant ID as spoken or keyed by the caller, digits only.

ani.description: Caller's phone number from get_call_context. Use on the first attempt.

postal_code.description: Business US zip code or Canadian postal code. Use on the second attempt.

name: get_account_status
description: Call this once, right after authenticate_merchant succeeds, and never before. Check the result in order and act on the first match: (1) collections_hold.active is true: call is_business_hours('collections'); if open, transfer to collections, otherwise continue to (2). (2) fraud_hold.active is true: if days_since_placed is 4 or less, read the recent-hold message using placed_date_spoken exactly as given; if more than 4, call is_business_hours('fraud') to choose between transferring to fraud and the email message. (3) bank_account_update_case.open is true: offer the verification callback. (4) Nothing applies: go to the main menu. Never explain why a hold exists or predict when funds will be released.

name: is_business_hours
description: Call this before any transfer to collections or fraud, and before offering the 'specialist' option. Specifically: when there is a collections hold; when a fraud hold is more than 4 days old; after any funds hold message, to decide whether to offer 'say specialist or press 2'; and when the caller asks for a person. If open is false, don't transfer or offer a specialist; tell the caller the hours using hours_spoken and offer the main menu. Don't call this for main menu service transfers.

name: create_callback_case
description: Call this only when get_account_status showed an open bank account update case, the caller said yes to choosing a callback time, and they picked a window: 'morning' or 1, 'midday' or 2, 'afternoon' or 3. Don't call it if they say skip, no, press star, or don't answer. Call it once per call. Then confirm with: 'Expect a call within the next 2 business days, between {window_spoken}.' Don't read the case_id aloud unless the caller asks for a reference number.

window.description: morning = 7 to 10 AM, midday = 10 AM to 2 PM, afternoon = 2 to 6 PM.

name: transfer
description: Call this to end your part of the call and hand the caller off, always after you've said the handoff line out loud. Use 'collections' for a collections hold during business hours. Use 'fraud' for a fraud hold more than 4 days old during business hours, when the caller says 'specialist' or presses 2 after a hold message, or when they ask for a person during business hours. Use a main menu queue once the caller's need is clear and you've confirmed it in one sentence ('Okay, connecting you with terminal support'). Never transfer to collections or fraud without is_business_hours returning open true. Call it once; after it succeeds, stop talking.

queue.description: collections and fraud are specialist queues. Main menu queues, with their keypad numbers: batch_transaction_deposit (2: batch, transaction, or deposit questions), terminal_support (3: terminal password, troubleshooting, paper supplies), statements_account_changes (4: statements, tax documents, authorized contacts, account information), disputes_chargebacks (5: disputes, chargebacks, 'Request for Transaction Documentation' letters), voice_authorization (6), government_public_sector (8: government or public sector customers).

reason.description: One line for the receiving agent: whether the caller was authenticated, the Merchant ID and business name, what you found, and what the caller wants. Example: 'Authenticated 4472190 Blue Fern Café; fraud hold placed Oct 28, 7 days in review; caller asked for specialist.' Never include full card or bank account numbers.
